Questions and answers
Questions about Android Automotive work
What is Android Automotive (AAOS), and how is it different from Android Auto?

Android Automotive OS (AAOS) is a version of Android that runs natively on the car's own infotainment system, so the apps live in the vehicle itself and no phone is needed. Android Auto is different: it runs on a connected phone and projects the phone's apps onto the car's screen. Building for Android Automotive means building for the vehicle, its screens and the systems behind them, rather than for a phone.
Has Vynatix shipped Android Automotive software to production?

Yes. In 2024 Vynatix rebuilt the in-cab radio and media player for Volvo Trucks on Android Automotive and shipped it to production across the fleet. It was built above the vehicle hardware layer, and the scope was agreed before the first line of code.
Do you work on site in Gothenburg?

Vynatix is based in Gothenburg, and the first conversation with a new client is usually in person here, face to face. After that our senior engineers work inside your team, and most of the work happens in writing, so there is a record you can read afterwards.
Can you work under an NDA with a vehicle maker?
Yes. Non-disclosure is normal in our work: beyond the cases published on this site, our work with Volvo Trucks and Volvo Cars is under non-disclosure.

Advice
The right tool for each problem
A language model is the right tool for reading and writing language: answering questions over documents, summarising, classifying, extracting details and drafting.
Ordinary code, a query or a search is the right tool when the answer has to be exact and the same every time, or when it already solves the problem.
So we choose the tool with you before you spend on a model. If a simpler one serves you better, we recommend it.
Often the better tool
Ordinary code or a database query, when the answer has to be exact
A rules engine, when the logic is already written down
Search, when people need the document rather than a summary of it
A form, when the input is structured anyway
Regulated client · <1>2025</1>
An assistant that answers only from approved documents.

For a regulated client, we built a closed-domain assistant that answers only from approved documents. Every answer cites its source. A question it cannot ground in source is declined and handed to a person, rather than answered with a guess.
<1>The boundary.</1> We set that line deliberately, and we can show you where it sits and why.
Evaluation and observability
How do you know the system is right?

You know because it is measured, before and after it ships: an evaluation pipeline tests every change against questions with known answers, and production observability shows what the system does with real questions.

<1>Before it ships.</1> An evaluation set is a collection of representative questions, each with the answer the system should give or the note that it should decline. The set is written with the people who know the domain. The pipeline runs it automatically whenever the model, the prompts, the retrieval or the documents change, and compares the result with the previous version, so a regression shows up before release rather than in front of a user.

<1>After it ships.</1> Observability means logging what was retrieved for each question, what the system answered and which source it cited, within your rules for how data may be handled. It also means following refusals, wrong answers, response times and cost over time. Failures found in production go back into the evaluation set, so the same mistake is tested for from then on.
Neither makes a model perfect. Together they make its errors visible and measurable, which is what lets you decide where the line should sit.

Frequently asked questions
What is RAG?

RAG (retrieval-augmented generation) is a technique in which the system first retrieves relevant passages from a document collection, such as your own documents, and then has a language model write the answer from those passages. Because the answer is built on retrieved passages, it can cite its source. The aim is for the facts in an answer to come from the documents rather than from the model's general training. That makes answers checkable, and you control what the assistant answers from by controlling which documents go in.
Can the system run on-prem or in a sovereign cloud?

Yes. Vynatix deploys AI systems into the client's own environment, including on-prem and sovereign cloud, as part of the AI engineering service, so the system can run where your data is allowed to be. Which model you can use then depends on what can run in that environment, and we say plainly what that choice means for quality.
Can the assistant refuse to answer outside the approved documents?

Yes. That is how the assistant Vynatix built in 2025 for a regulated client works: it answers only from approved documents, every answer cites its source, and a question it cannot ground in source is declined and handed to a person. The line was set deliberately, and we can show where it sits and why.
Do you build MCP servers?

Yes. Vynatix builds MCP servers and integrations as part of its AI engineering work. MCP (Model Context Protocol) is an open protocol that lets an AI assistant or agent call your tools and read your data through a defined interface. The server decides what is made available, so access is explicit and can be limited.

How to choose a software consultancy, Vynatix
Guide

Choose a software consultancy by how it works: the people you meet should be the people who do the work, you should own the code, and the hours should be reported openly. Vynatix, the senior software consultancy for scale-ups, wrote this guide.
Published <1>6 November 2026</1> · Last updated <2>20 November 2026</2> · Vynatix

What decides most is who actually does the work and what you are left with when the engagement is over. Hourly rate and firm size say little about the result. The checklist below works whichever firm you choose.
What should you settle before you contact a consultancy?

Before you contact anyone, settle four things: the outcome you want, the constraint that cannot be negotiated away, roughly what budget you have, and what you can already do yourselves. Write them down, so that the first call is concrete and the answers are easy to compare.
<1>The outcome:</1> what should work when the engagement ends, described clearly enough that someone outside the team could say whether it has been reached.
<1>The hard constraint:</1> a deadline, a rule you must follow, a platform you cannot change, or data that cannot leave the building.
<1>The budget range:</1> a range is enough for a firm to tell you whether the engagement is realistic.
<1>What you already have:</1> the skills in your team, and who on your side will own the result afterwards.
Consultancy, consultant broker or your own hire: which fits when?

A consultancy fits when you want someone to take responsibility for a defined delivery, a consultant broker when you know exactly which role you need to fill and can lead the work yourself, and your own hire when the need is long term and part of your core business. None of them is better in general, and you can combine them.

Which questions should you ask a software consultancy?

Ask who does the work, how senior they are, who owns the code, how the work is documented, how hours are reported, what is out of scope and how the engagement ends. Notice which answers come slowly or turn vague.
<1>Who does the work?</1> Meet the developers who will work on the engagement, and ask whether they will be the same people once the contract is signed.
<1>How senior are they?</1> Ask what they have built that went into production and what they were personally responsible for.
<1>Who owns the code?</1> The answer should be you, from the first day, with documentation and access to everything you need to carry on without the firm.
<1>How is the work documented?</1> Ask for an example of what an earlier engagement left behind.
<1>How are hours reported?</1> Ask how often and at what level of detail.
<1>What is out of scope?</1> A firm that has understood the task can say where the boundary is and write it down before work starts.
<1>How does the engagement end?</1> Ask how the handover works and who on your side takes over.
How do you judge whether the developers are really senior?

You judge seniority best by talking technology directly with the person who will do the work and asking to see something they have written. Years on a CV say less than how someone reasons about trade-offs and constraints.
Ask for something they have written and are allowed to show, such as a design note or a handover document. It shows whether the next developer could understand the work.
Ask about an engagement they turned down, and why. A senior developer knows where their own ability ends.
Describe a real problem from your own work and listen for the follow-up questions. Someone who asks about the constraints before proposing a solution has usually done similar work before.
Warning signs
Which warning signs should you take seriously?

Treat it as a warning when you cannot meet the person who will do the work, when someone else turns up after the contract is signed, or when nobody will write down what is included. Each can have an innocent explanation. Together they usually mean that nobody takes responsibility for the result.
Watch for
A salesperson or account manager between you and the developer, whom you cannot get past
A different CV after the contract is signed
A scope that nobody will write down
A yes to everything, without a single limit
Invoices that cannot be matched against reported hours

What is the difference between a software consultancy and a consultant broker?

A consultancy has its own developers and stands behind their work, while a consultant broker places consultants from other companies, or self-employed consultants, into a role that you lead yourself. The contract decides where responsibility for the result sits, but with a broker it usually sits with you.
Who should own the code when a consultancy has written it?
You should own the code from the first day, and the contract should say so. This is not legal advice, so have someone who knows contracts read the terms.
How do you check that the consultants are senior?

Talk technology directly with the developers who will do the work, ask for something they have written, and ask about an engagement they turned down and why. How they reason about constraints says more than the number of years on a CV.
When is hiring your own team better than using consultants?

Hiring your own team is usually better when the need is long term and the skill is part of your core business. Consultants fit better when the need is limited in time, or when you need experience that you do not have time to build yourselves.
How should hours be reported on a consulting engagement?
Hours should be reported regularly, preferably every week, and in enough detail for you to see what the time was spent on. The invoice should be possible to check against the report.
